sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Roman-Germanic legal tradition) with unitary national company law regime and no sub-state tax autonomy
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US–Luxembourg Income and Capital Tax Treaty of 3 April 1996 (in force 20 December 2000; Business Profits and Royalties articles govern US B2B SaaS cross-border flows)
Germany–Luxembourg Double Taxation Agreement (as amended, including 2012 Protocol) applicable to EU enterprise software distribution
China–Luxembourg Bilateral Investment Treaty of 1985 (protection of investments; relevant for Asian investor chains)
EU internal market freedoms combined with EU–Japan EPA and EU FTA network (B2B software trade in EU framework)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (Loi RCS), as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Luxembourg company law); CSSF Regulation No 20-01 of 11 May 2020 on AML/CFT supervision; EBA Guidelines on beneficial ownership identification. The Luxembourg RBE is a non-public register: access is limited to competent authorities, the Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers), AML/CFT obliged entities performing customer due diligence, and persons demonstrating legitimate interest, following the ECJ rulings in C-37/20 and C-601/20.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each beneficial owner and statutory manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport authority of country of origin; Luxembourg notary or registered certification agent in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Luxembourg acceded 1978; apostille issued by the designated authority of the document's country of origin; consular legalization required only for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record / police clearance (extrait de casier judiciaire) of managers and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National criminal records office / judicial authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn translation into French/German/Luxembourgish if not in one of those languages

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of address / residence certificate of each UBO (recent utility bill, tax assessment, or municipal registry certificate)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal authority or regulated utility provider of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for municipal certificates; bank-issued certificates generally accepted as banker's confirmation without apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate excerpt / certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder, plus board resolution authorizing incorporation of the Luxembourg SARL
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official commercial register of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; certified translation into French, German, or Luxembourgish where the issuing state is not a Hague Convention member, consular legalization at the Luxembourg embassy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and continuous screening of UBOs, managers, authorized signatories, and commercial counterparties against: (i) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, (ii) UN Security Council sanctions lists, (iii) US OFAC SDN list and related OFAC sanctions programs in accordance with Luxembourg banking practice, (iv) Luxembourg FIU/CRF red-flag indicators and national judicial freezing orders, and (v) adverse media and Politically Exposed Persons (foreign, domestic, and international organization) classifications per EBA Guidelines and CSSF Regulation No 20-01. PEPs trigger enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval; B2B Enterprise SaaS is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, but screening and documentary records must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — official company registry portal for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible at www.lbr.lu; name reservation filed through the LBR e-requests module (LBR anything)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Luxembourg language regime (Law of 24 February 1984), the articles of association and the registered name may be drafted in French, German, or Luxembourgish; French dominates in standard practice. The corporate name must be expressed in Latin-script characters and must include the legal-form suffix 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the recognized abbreviation 'S.à r.l.'/'SARL'. Foreign words are admissible only where non-misleading and clearly distinguishable from existing RCS names; the RCS conducts exact-match and confusing-similarity checks against the national name index, including prior trade names and protected designations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société d'investissement / OPCVM / UCITS / Fonds de pension
Luxembourg / Luxembourgeois — requires prior authorization of the Minister of the Economy under the Law of 31 July 1937
Université / Académie / École royale (protected educational designations)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS issues a negative name availability decision (avis négatif), the applicant receives a reasoned refusal in the LBR portal. Counsel must file an amended reservation within 15 days using a materially distinguishing prefix, suffix, or domain-style addition. Where refusal persists on grounds of public order, misleading character, or prohibited tokens, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal addressed to the LBR registry officers through the e-request channel, and thereafter may initiate judicial review (recours) before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within the statutory time limit for judicial appeals against registry decisions; legal and notarial advice should be obtained before filing. No automatic extension of the 60-day reservation exists; an expired reservation requires a new filing and renewal of the statutory tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Only an approved domiciliation agent licensed under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, as amended, may provide a virtual/domiciliation address. For a B2B Enterprise SaaS SARL, a pure virtual office is discouraged: Luxembourg tax administration, EU ATAD/CBCR substance expectations, and VAT fixed-establishment rules require genuine local substance (manager presence, board-level decision-making, IT oversight, and transparent invoicing). A regulated domiciliation address combined with demonstrable substance is acceptable at incorporation stage, but must be upgraded to a physical operating office before active cross-border SaaS contracts are concluded.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15–20% in the first fiscal year for a low-risk technology SARL; likelihood increases materially above 50% where the company exhibits letterbox indicators, repeated B2B cross-border flows to non-transparent jurisdictions, inconsistent UBO filings, or minimal substance. Unannounced inspections may be performed by the Administration des Contributions Directes (direct tax), the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (VAT/registration), the CSSF within its AML supervisory remit, and the Luxembourg FIU.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name availability check and statutory name reservation (validated through LBR e-request)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR fee schedule (EUR 15 per reservation request)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: KYC/UBO verification and AML/CFT vetting of shareholders, UBOs, and managers by counsel and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / notary / domiciliation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (range USD 500–1,300 per customer due diligence file)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille and consular legalization of UBO passports, police certificates, corporate excerpts, and address proofs (estimated three documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated Hague Apostille authorities of document origin / Luxembourg embassies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document fees of issuing states (USD 60–120 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation of the SARL (cash share capital, single or multi-shareholder standard deed)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff regulated by Grand-Ducal regulation plus prevailing market benchmark (EUR 1,500–2,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS electronic registration and publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory exemption: no filing or publication fee for fully electronic filings since 1 June 2016

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial owner declaration filing with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory exemption: RBE filing is free of charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / authorized domiciliation initial three-month advance under the Law of 31 May 1999
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation agent or commercial landlord
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for substance-compliant office solutions (USD 300–500 per month)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Incorporation legal counsel fee (articles of association drafting, board minutes, UBO registers, preliminary Luxembourg direct tax and VAT opinion for US/EU B2B SaaS invoicing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a low-risk SARL (USD 2,000–4,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation of foreign-issued document bundles into French, German, or Luxembourgish, if required
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 45–70 per standard page (estimated four pages)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 1-10, 50-55 and 57-68 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the accounting duties of undertakings; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 on the RCS electronic filing procedure.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR-RCS), operated under the authority of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif de la Société à Responsabilité Limitée) submitted electronically through the e-RCS portal using RCS Form E1.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000.00 fully subscribed; at incorporation each share must be paid up to at least 25% of its nominal value, and any share premium must be fully paid; the paid-up capital must be deposited in a blocked company escrow account (compte bloqué) opened at a Luxembourg credit institution, and the bank's blocked-funds certificate is annexed to the notarial deed before registration with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the first meeting of the shareholders and managers of the SARL, duly assembled on the date of incorporation: RESOLVED that the subscription of 100 registered shares with par value EUR 120.00 each, fully subscribed in the amount of EUR 12,000.00, is approved; each shareholder confirms the deposit of no less than 25% of the nominal value into the company's blocked bank account established with a Luxembourg credit institution, as evidenced by the blocked-funds certificate. RESOLVED further that the registered office is adopted at [address], Luxembourg, and the articles of incorporation are ratified. RESOLVED further that [Name] is appointed sole manager (gérant) with individual signature authority, and is authorised to complete all registry filings and licencing applications.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked share-capital account and deposit of paid-up capital at a Luxembourg credit institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg credit institution supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a licensed Luxembourg bank; open a blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the future company; deposit at least 25% of the EUR 12,000 minimum subscribed capital, i.e. a minimum of EUR 3,000, and any full share premium; instruct the bank to issue a blocked-funds attestation addressed to the notary attesting the irrevocable availability of the funds until the completion of registration.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association
Passport or national identity card of each shareholder and proposed manager
Proof of residential address for each founder
KYC and AML forms of the credit institution
Beneficial ownership self-declaration form
LEI or identification data of corporate shareholders, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the purpose of the account or requests supplementary KYC evidence, resubmit the corrected formation project and identification documents; if the blocked-funds certificate is defective, obtain a corrected attestation from the bank; alternative remedy is to open the blocked account at another CSSF-licensed bank and produce a new certificate before notarisation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial incorporation deed and adoption of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary registered with the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg (Duchy of Luxembourg Chamber of Notaries)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the selected Luxembourg notary with the draft articles of association and the blocked-funds certificate; the notary authenticates the acte constitutif, verifies the identity and capacity of each shareholder and manager, confirms the fully subscribed minimum capital and the paid-up fraction, and records the corporate object of developing enterprise cloud software and SaaS applications (ISIC 6201); all founders or their duly appointed proxy holders must sign the deed personally before the notary.
required_dossiers: Blocked-funds certificate issued by the Luxembourg bank
Draft articles of association (charter)
Original identification documents of shareholders, managers and proxy holders
Power of attorney notarised if a shareholder signs by proxy
RCS pre-registration name reservation receipt, if obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects a drafting defect before execution, amend the statutes and proceed to signature on the same day; if an error is discovered after execution, execute a notarial rectificatory instrument (acte rectificatif) before filing the RCS application, and attach the corrective deed to the e-RCS submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the SARL with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) — Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the e-RCS secure portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the notarial deed, complete RCS Form E1 electronically on the e-RCS portal; attach a certified copy of the notarial deed, the correct legal form (SARL), the registered office address, the corporate object, the gérant's identity and signature powers, and the beneficial ownership details; pay the EUR 19 electronic filing fee online and acknowledge the automatic transmission for publication; the RCS will issue the registration number and the official extract evidencing legal personality.
required_dossiers: Authentic copy of the notarial incorporation deed
Completed RCS Form E1 / E1bis
Identification data and specimen signatures of the appointed manager (gérant)
Beneficial ownership register natural-person declarations
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query for missing or inconsistent data, respond within the prescribed period through the e-RCS task inbox, uploading supplementary documents or a corrective filing; if the one-month statutory term is exceeded, file immediately and pay the administrative late-filing fee, and attach an explanatory statement to mitigate any sanction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the incorporation deed in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de la Justice — Legilux RESA electronic compendium, operated with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS assigns the registration number, the official abstract of the notarial deed is transmitted automatically for publication in RESA at a fee of approximately EUR 19.20; monitor the RESA portal for the publication certificate; publication grants opposability of the incorporation deed and officer appointments to third parties under Article 1912 of the Law of 10 August 1915.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarial deed abstract authenticated by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice contains typographical or translation errors, request an erratum publication through the LBR portal and, if required, execute a rectificatory notarial deed; if the publication is delayed beyond the statutory period, contact the LBR helpdesk with the RCS number to trigger manual publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration regulatory activation — VAT, direct taxes, social security and business establishment licence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income tax and municipal business tax; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes, Ministère de l'Économie, for the autorisation d'établissement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Luxembourg VAT by filing the eTVA registration application within 15 days after the effective start of operations, using the company's RCS extract to obtain the LU VAT number; register the SARL with the CCSS via the EDISS/EDV portal for employer duties; file the autorisation d'établissement application with the Ministry of the Economy business licence one-stop shop if the company will exercise a commercial, artisanal, industrial or liberal professional activity in or from Luxembourg; notify the ACD for corporate income tax and municipal business tax assessment using the RCS extract.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Certified copy of the notarial deed and articles of association
Identity document of the appointed manager (gérant)
Lease agreement or ownership title for the registered office
Business plan or activity description for the establishment licence file
Bank account confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT application is suspended for incomplete details, respond to the AEDT within the set time limit and resubmit the missing data; if the business licence application is refused or queried, provide the requested documentation through the Ministry's one-stop window or appeal the decision to the Tribunal administratif within three months of notice; any late VAT or tax registration is cured by prompt filing and payment of interest, with a possible request for remission of surcharges.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie — Direction Générale du Commerce, de l'Industrie et des Classes Moyennes (Department for Business Establishment Licensing)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement — Business / Establishment Licence issued under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and certain liberal professions

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category III administrative activity; software development and SaaS office premises do not appear on the Annex to the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment or the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 January 2018; no formal EIA report or environmental registration is required unless the activity expands into a colocation or data-centre facility exceeding the relevant Annex thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No manufacturing discharge: office operations must comply with municipal wastewater and stormwater connection standards; IT hardware disposal must follow the WEEE regime under the Law of 21 March 2017 and Directive 2012/19/EU; VOC and dust emissions are effectively nil, while any standby generators or cooling units must respect the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 16 June 2011 on ambient noise and the municipal ordinance on acoustic limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: the leased premises must obtain a favourable fire-prevention review by the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) and the municipal safety commission, including the evacuation plan, fire alarm and extinguishing systems; Structural: an occupancy certificate or building licence (certificat d'occupation) confirming structural load capacity and safety conformity; Occupational: registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), a documented workplace risk assessment, verification of electrical installations, adequate welfare facilities, and first-aid arrangements as required by the Labour Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; unified digital portal MyGuichet (myguichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities registering for VAT must complete form 640/TVA, submit proof of incorporation, copy of statutes, and a power of attorney. Non-EU companies must appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative accepted by AEDT. For corporate income tax, registration with ACD follows incorporation with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), including filing of annual accounts, director identification, and appointment of an approved auditor when applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: VAT grouping (assujetti unique) election under Article 62 of the VAT Law; optional small undertaking exemption election under Article 57 (annual turnover below EUR 35,000); tax consolidation election for resident subsidiaries under the CIT Law. No check-the-box election exists; hybrid mismatch notifications apply under ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for existing small undertakings (exemption); new undertakings must not project first-year turnover above EUR 25,000. Distance sales into Luxembourg exceeding EUR 100,000 trigger registration; no threshold applies to non-established suppliers making taxable B2B supplies in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL (UBL/CII); no compulsory domestic B2B real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime in force as of 2025. E-invoices are acceptable provided the authenticity of origin and integrity of content are guaranteed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exports of goods to non-EU countries where the exporter possesses a customs export declaration and evidenced dispatch from EU territory within three months. B2B services supplied to a customer established outside the EU are outside Luxembourg VAT when the customer possesses a non-EU VAT identification number and actual use and enjoyment occurs outside the EU. Intra-Community supplies are also zero-rated with the customer's EU VAT ID and Intrastat filing where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Transport documents (CMR / Bill of Lading / Air Waybill)
Proof of payment (SWIFT / Bank transfer certificate)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT authorities may retroactively adjust zero-rating for up to four years when export substantiation is incomplete. Reassessment carries interest at 0.8% per month, a civil fine of 10% of the VAT amount, and monetary penalties up to EUR 4,000. Fraudulent export refund claims trigger clawback of refunded VAT, joint liability under Article 73 VAT Law, and criminal prosecution with potential imprisonment in cases of serious VAT fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and, with delegated prudential supervision, Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and financial instruments
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full euro-area member with complete current account and capital account convertibility under the EC Treaties and the EU Capital Movement Directive (2015/2361). There are no exchange control restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, shareholder loans, or capital repatriation. A SARL may freely maintain accounts in EUR or any foreign currency, although statutory accounts must be presented in EUR for filing. Withholding tax leakage on dividends is reduced by tax treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. No prior central bank approval is required for inbound or outbound transfers, subject only to reporting thresholds for balance-of-payments statistics and anti-money laundering verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement in Luxembourg. All export receipts in convertible currencies may be retained, sold, or hedged at the exporter's discretion. Settlement of export invoices is subject to the general AML/CFT transaction monitoring rules of the CSSF and requires accurate economic purpose and underlying commercial documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EUR or multi-currency) for routine SaaS B2B collections and vendor payments; a separate Capital Escrow Account may be opened for a contributed share capital block pending final registration.
Operational Account with integrated treasury services and cross-currency clearing; Capital Escrow Account acceptable for share capital deposits under notarial deeds.
Operational Account and Wealth / Corporate Treasury Account; Capital Escrow Account for reserved capital increase deposits.
Operational Account for small-mid corporate treasury and trade settlement; Capital Escrow Account available with simplified domestic procedures.
Operational Account with strong cross-border B2B payment corridors; Capital Escrow Account accepted for institutional seed capital structures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High for EU-authorized Electronic Money Institutions passported into Luxembourg under PSD2 (e.g., Wise or Revolut Business) for operational EUR transfers. For non-EU offshore digital EMIs, the legal constraint is significant: they may not hold a bank license in Luxembourg, cannot provide lending or safeguarded investment products, and are normally rejected for high-value treasury clearing because they lack a Luxembourg branch or CSSF passport. If the SaaS company needs commercial bank-grade counterparty risk, an EU EMI is complements a T1 bank account rather than replacing one.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg banks generally require the physical presence of at least one authorized director and the ultimate beneficial owner(s) (UBO) at the initial client acceptance interview unless an introduction from a regulated EU credit institution or notary allows remote onboarding under CSSF circular-based risk assessment. Many T1 banks now accept video-identification via a regulated third-party provider, but a physical meeting with a relationship manager, or a certified notarial copy of corporate documents, remains the dominant default for a first-time corporate client. For full remote opening, the client must normally provide a signed power-of-attorney to a Luxembourg-based contact person and pass an enhanced due diligence review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO is a tax-resident in a high-risk jurisdiction or has a politically exposed person (PEP) status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized source-of-wealth declaration, audited personal tax returns for the prior three years, bank statements from a reputable EU/EEA bank, and a detailed explanation of the corporate shareholding chain with all intermediate UBO verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound initial capital is considered disproportionate to the declared business plan or economic profile of the SaaS entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan with revenue projections, signed client contracts or letters of intent, proof of funding source (e.g., investor bank account), and a capital call schedule conforming to the notarial deed and Luxembourg Company Law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate cross-border disbursement to a non-EU vendor or supplier without a commercial underlying
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date commercial contracts, vendor invoices, proof of delivery or completed milestones, transfer-pricing documentation where relevant, and a tax legal opinion confirming substance requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a high-risk jurisdiction as the destination for SaaS license fees or intercompany royalty payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full IP ownership chain, valuation report under the arm's-length principle, double tax treaty analysis, and a Luxembourg substance file with board minutes prepared by a local tax adviser.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared ISIC activity (software publishing) and expected incoming payment patterns, such as immediate outbound transfers to treasury centers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The SaaS licensing model, customer contracts, technical documentation of the IT service, employee/payroll evidence, and a legal memorandum explaining commercial rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions (share capital or shareholder loans) are wired via SWIFT MT103 to the SARL's euro-denominated account at a Luxembourg Bank. The wire must cite the bank's required reference fields: Beneficiary Legal Name, VAT/EIN if applicable, and the payment purpose code covering 'Inbound capital injection' (under the ECS/BCL external statistics classification). For share capital, the type code 'S030' (equity securities) or the ECB Balance-of-Payments event code for cross-border equity injection should be used; a copy of the notarised share subscription deed and the RCS registration excerpt must be retained. The sending financial institution should include the full corporate identifier and the specific mention 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' in the field 70 (Remittance Information). The BCL requires the receiving bank to report the transaction in the balance-of-payments statistic when the amount exceeds EUR 12,500; however, no prior regulatory authorization is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for B2B SaaS (licensing, intercompany royalties, cloud infrastructure charges) are cleared primarily via SWIFT MT103 (for non-SEPA / non-EUR currencies) or SEPA Instant / SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the EEA. Where a commercial invoice is backed by a bank payment guarantee, the SARL may use a Documentary Collection or an Irrevocable Confirmed Commercial Letter of Credit. The MT103 must include the proper remittance information, the underlying invoice numbers, and the contractual references. For large infrastructure payments to non-EU cloud providers, the bank will conduct a sanctions screening and check the counterparty; the SARL should prepare a supporting file containing the supplier contract, invoice breakdown, and the appropriate OECD Transfer Pricing documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, or EUR/CHF executed with a Luxembourg bank under an ISDA 1992 or ISDA 2002 Master Agreement
FX swaps (foreign exchange swap) for simultaneous spot and forward value settlement in two currencies
Currency options (European style) purchased for downside protection on high-volume USD receivables
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for matching a fixed-rate USD asset with a EUR liability profile
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for restricted currencies pursuant to the bank's internal product policy and the Luxembourg regulator's derivative licensing requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts filing (statutory accounts, directors' report and auditor's report when applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting approval within six months of financial year end; deposit with the RCS within one month after approval; for a 31 December year-end the practical window runs through 31 July of the next year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes managers to coercive fines and civil/criminal sanctions, administrative strike-off after continued default, and refusal by the RCS to issue a certificate of good standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (UBO file update and confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: confirm RBE data in the calendar month of the anniversary of the relevant UBO declaration, and re-file within one month of any direct or indirect shareholding transfer changing beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 125,000 for legal entities and up to EUR 62,500 or imprisonment for individuals; each incomplete or false declaration is separately sanctionable; administrative strike-off can follow failure to comply with judicial injunctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax return (Model 400)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Direct Tax Authority of Luxembourg)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 March of the following tax year; e-filing through MyGuichet typically extends the deadline to 31 December of the following year for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.8% per month on unpaid balances, late-filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax due, mandatory late-filing charge, and ex officio assessment; criminal sanctions for deliberate non-filing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit for SARL when at least two of three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average number of employees 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in force under the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and the amended Law of 25 May 2021 relating to accounting and annual accounts (transposition of EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU is also permitted for unlisted companies under certain conditions

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every shareholding transfer, including a direct change in shareholder into the SARL's share register, is recorded in the Register of Members; within one month of the transfer the SARL must file the resulting beneficial ownership change with the RBE; each year the SARL must reconfirm the exactness of all RBE information as at the anniversary date in the corresponding civil month, and the confirmation is evidenced by an updated shareholding list in the statutory Register of Members
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des Associés/SARL share ledger)
Minute Book of shareholder and management resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - USD 4,000 per year for a Luxembourg registered office/domiciliation and corporate agent at mid-market Luxembourg pricing
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - USD 25,000 per year for the statutory audit of a small SARL at current Luxembourg fee levels

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC) for tax year 2024/2025; plus 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC (1.19 percentage points) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, 6.75% in Luxembourg City), giving an aggregate headline burden of 24.94% for Luxembourg City companies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box (Art. 50bis LIR): 80% exemption of net qualifying income derived from software copyrights and other qualifying IP, producing an effective aggregate tax rate of approximately 4.99% in Luxembourg City; Notional Interest Deduction on new qualifying equity contributions; Investment Tax Credit (crédit d'impôt pour investissement) for eligible depreciable assets; no dividend withholding tax on large qualifying EU corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory time limit (perpetual carryforward); annual offset is capped at 90% of taxable income exceeding EUR 200,000 per tax year (Art. 110/111 LIR).
